# Findings (auto-generated by analysis.py)

Every number below is computed from `db/analytics_jobs.db`. Salary figures = postings with a usable salary (1 LPA - 1 Cr, annualised), median LPA unless stated.

**Sample:** 4,508 analytics postings; 999 (22%) have a usable salary. Salary conclusions describe *disclosed* salaries only.

## 3. Skill premium (996 salary postings)

Log-salary regression with role, experience and experience squared held fixed. `role_only` = same model without experience. `lo`/`hi` = 95% bootstrap interval of `role_plus_exp`. `clear` = interval excludes 0.

| skill | n_with | role_only | role_plus_exp | lo | hi | clear |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| excel | 156 | -49% | -35% | -43% | -27% | yes |
| azure | 183 | +1% | -10% | -20% | +1% | no |
| snowflake | 82 | -1% | -4% | -14% | +7% | no |
| sql | 345 | -2% | -1% | -9% | +7% | no |
| spark | 296 | -2% | -1% | -12% | +12% | no |
| machine learning | 130 | -3% | +4% | -12% | +21% | no |
| python | 411 | +3% | +7% | -2% | +16% | no |

| aws | 207 | +23% | +12% | +2% | +23% | yes |
| power bi | 124 | +35% | +16% | +3% | +30% | yes |

Model R-squared (in-sample): 0.63.

## 4. Salary model (5-fold cross-validated R-squared on log salary)

| features | model | cv_r2 | sd |
|---|---|---|---|
| Role only | Ridge | 0.34 | 0.06 |
| Role only | Random forest | 0.34 | 0.06 |
| Role + experience | Ridge | 0.56 | 0.07 |
| Role + experience | Random forest | 0.61 | 0.05 |
| + skills | Ridge | 0.6 | 0.05 |
| + skills | Random forest | 0.65 | 0.03 |
| + skills + city | Ridge | 0.6 | 0.05 |
| + skills + city | Random forest | 0.65 | 0.04 |

Importance by feature group (drop in R-squared when shuffled):

| group | r2_drop | sd |
|---|---|---|
| Experience | 0.678 | 0.06 |
| Skills (10 core) | 0.122 | 0.027 |
| Role | 0.074 | 0.017 |
| City | 0.034 | 0.015 |

## Limits to quote in the README

- Salary is disclosed in only ~22% of postings; results describe disclosed salaries.
- Skill tags are capped at 8 per posting, so a skill can be asked for but missing from the data.
- Skill effects are associations in observed postings, not proof that learning a skill raises pay.
- Role is assigned from the title only; roughly 20 titles per role were eyeballed, not formally measured.
- Snapshot of ~20 days, so no time trends.
